source.title: DP-AdamBC: Your DP-Adam Is Actually DP-SGD (Unless You Apply Bias Correction)
source.authors: Qiao-Yue Tang; Frederick Shpilevskiy; M. L'ecuyer

record.tranche_reason: The study directly compares differentially private Adam, bias-corrected Adam, and DP-SGD, and argues that privacy noise can make DP-Adam behave like DP-SGD with momentum. It refines optimizer-generalization claims in a privacy-sensitive setting; it does not test the listed natural-label, non-private optimizer comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper reports train/test loss and test accuracy for optimizer comparisons, as well as a measurement of the relationship between DP-Adam and DP-SGD. Its DP-SGD and DP-Adam results are included as comparators; results cited from other work, including the sign-descent hypothesis, are not extracted as this study's findings. Hyperparameter values used only for tuning are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own DP-Adam versus DP-SGD held-out accuracy comparisons on image and text classification, extending V4 to private training. It tunes numerical stability constants and, in some experiments, additional training parameters, so it does not reproduce V4's limited-tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors attribute DP-Adam's altered updates to noise bias in its second-moment estimate and show that, when this bias dominates, it approximates DP-SGDM with a derived schedule. They recommend DP-AdamBC particularly for tasks suited to Adam and emphasize tuning sensitivity. The conclusion should also acknowledge that DP-AdamBC beats both baselines on ogbn-arxiv at epsilon≈3 and ≈6, despite showing little benefit at epsilon≈12.
record.recipe_differences: Uses differential privacy with gradient clipping and added noise, and compares DP-Adam with a bias-corrected variant and DP-SGD; it is not the non-private optimizer comparison in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset/task, privacy budget, batch size/noise setting, and optimizer hyperparameter tuning (including γ′) affect the reported outcomes. On text tasks DP-AdamBC improves over DP-Adam; on CIFAR10 and ogbn-arxiv the improvement is minor or absent. The DP-Adam/DP-SGDM training comparison is reported closer for larger Φ.

fits_no_version.finding: DP-AdamBC improves over DP-Adam on several text classification tasks, with smaller or absent gains on the other tested tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Correcting differential privacy noise bias in Adam's second-moment estimate can improve private classification accuracy, depending on task and tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: The graph-classification comparisons use different DP-SGD and adaptive-optimizer architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Private graph-classification accuracy depends on the combined architecture and optimization recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: DP-Adam and DP-SGDM with a derived learning-rate schedule have closely aligned trajectories, especially when privacy noise dominates the second moment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Privacy noise can make DP-Adam approximate momentum SGD with a particular learning-rate schedule.

record.problems: The optimizer comparison is under differential privacy, so it does not directly establish the listed non-private optimizer claims. Results depend on per-optimizer tuning, and the authors identify γ′ as an important hyperparameter. Some trajectory comparisons are figure-only without exact values. For DP-GCN, the DP-SGD architecture differs from the DP-Adam/DP-AdamBC architecture.
record.rows_left_out: No reported table rows omitted. The paper's comparisons against DP2-RMSProp were not extracted because DP2 is a different method and those comparisons do not measure the claimed optimizer behaviors. Figure-only trajectories besides the DP-Adam versus DP-SGDM training comparison were not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same training recipe.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Non-private training; tuning restricted to learning rates and decay schedules; a controlled expansion of tuning budgets; decoupled weight decay; switching Adam to SGD; word-level language modeling. The accuracy comparisons do not establish equal or better training performance.
Controlled batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that remove a batch penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus random examples.

missing.what: DP-Adam versus DP-SGD accuracy at the lower privacy budgets: SNLI epsilon≈1 and ≈3; QNLI epsilon≈1 and ≈3; CIFAR10 epsilon≈1 and ≈3. Include the five-run standard deviations. These show both an SNLI ranking reversal across privacy budgets and persistent CIFAR10 disadvantage. R9 lacks the SGD baseline. The record incorrectly says no table rows were omitted.
missing.locator: Section 5, Table 1; Appendix D, Additional Experiments

record.verdict_notes: Private training is a new setting bearing on V4, rather than grounds for excluding every optimizer comparison. However, additional tuning, direct selection for test accuracy, and privacy constraints limit transfer to the original limited-tuning experiments. Improvements of the proposed method alone do not support V4. No result tests V1–V3 or V5–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Non-private comparisons; the listed broad benchmark comparison and language-model exception. This study compares DP optimizers under privacy constraints.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
